newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU diplomats sketch out likely EMU pact accord.
newsitem.headline: EU diplomats sketch out likely EMU pact accord.

text.p: European Union finance ministers on Monday were putting the finishing touches to a compromise plan to meet France's concerns that not enough attention is being paid to employment issues.
Diplomats said the likely agreement would include the following:
-- A decision to issue a Council Resolution by the EU heads of state and government. A fairly rare occurrence, a resolution carries no legal weight but carries a very heavy political signal.
-- The resolution would include language designed to redirect EU policy, most likely drawing on previous EU utterances on the issue.
-- It would also try to meet France's concerns over political control under economic and monetary union (EMU) by fleshing out current EU treaty language on economic coordination.

-- No new money for jobs projects would be included, but the European Investment Bank (EIB) may be given a broader mandate to lend funds to small businesses for job creation. Using EIB profits for jobs has also been discussed.

-- There would be a promise to study various other options for jobs funding within the current EU budget. Money in the EU's European Coal and Steel Community budget was one option, but a number of countries wanted the money used, if at all, only for job creation in those sectors.
-- The Stability Pact itself would not be changed in any way.

-- Leaders were likely to call separately for a special EU jobs summit to be held in Luxembourg in October. Luxembourg which takes over the EU presidency on July 1 has agreed in principle to host a summit, but officials say they want a clear indication of what exactly it would do.
